items.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025
items.q: I think that comes with him playing with Miles Davis... I heard about Miles Davis. So I went backwards in time

ctx.x: Musicians, jazz players especially, talk about being in the moment. When you say respond to things, can you describe how that works to people who don’t really understand it?

Well we all know a language, a basic language. We’ve all grown up playing song forms, we’ve, you know, touched base on playing with no song form. Now song form what I mean is a definite set of rules that we play with. And we all know a lot of the same song forms. So you could be in the country like Japan and not be able to speak a word to a guy but you start playing “Autumn Leaves” and everybody knows what to do immediately. And we go off of, for instance if I think of “Autumn Leaves” I think of Miles Davis…

another great thing that we have on the bandstand is space. And how to use space. So a great horn player will leave space for the rhythm section to do something with it. So that’s our opportunity. Now there’s three other rhythm section members normally that are participating you know. So you’ve got to be sensitive as to when to jump and do your thing you know. But you could be a leader of, you know, this movement, or you can stand back and go for the ride you know.
